page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-96 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine configured with eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a total of 192 GB of VRAM. The system is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor featuring 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by lower scores in stress-ng single-core tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core evaluations. Conversely, multi-core and parallelized execution is highly robust. The instance achieves strong results in multi-core stress-ng benchmarks, PassMark extended instructions, and Redis SET operations, which reached 63.66 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, particularly for cached small-block reads, which peaked at 4,211.44 GB/sec.

The primary strength of the g2-standard-96 lies in its GPU-accelerated compute capabilities, specifically for large language model (LLM) workloads. Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in prompt processing speeds across small, medium, and large models, with the medium 7B model processing prompts at 2,692.08 tokens per second. Text generation for medium and large models also ranks highly, making this server highly efficient for transformer-based workloads and parallelized AI inference.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-96 represents a high-density GPU resource allocation. It is optimized for enterprise-scale AI inference, machine learning model deployment, and parallel data processing where the cost of multiple discrete GPU instances can be consolidated into a single high-capacity node. However, the lower single-core performance suggests it is poorly suited for single-threaded legacy applications or workloads that do not leverage its multi-core or GPU hardware. Recommended workloads include LLM serving, multi-stream video processing, high-throughput database operations, and parallelized scientific simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-96 is a graphics-optimized server designed for high-density GPU workloads and parallel computing. It features eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs with a total of 192 GB of VRAM, paired with 96 vCPUs on an Intel Xeon x86_64 architecture and 384.0 GB of system memory. While single-core CPU performance is modest, the instance excels in multi-threaded operations and memory bandwidth, with cached small-block reads reaching 4,211.44 GB/sec. Benchmark results highlight top-tier capabilities in large language model prompt processing and text generation across various model sizes. Lacking local storage, this server is highly optimized for GPU-accelerated workloads, including AI inference, machine learning, and parallel data processing, offering a consolidated high-density hardware profile for demanding enterprise applications.
